name: disk_summary
title: Disk summary
description: Overview of Sōji's disk index: bytes indexed, how many folders it couldn't read, the largest items, and what grew lately.

name: largest_items
title: Largest items under a path
description: The largest folders and files under a path, by allocated size, from the index.

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: list_folder
title: List a folder
description: A folder's direct children with their sizes, from the index (or read from disk when the folder isn't indexed).

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: path_info
title: About a path
description: One path: allocated size, modified and created dates, folder or file, Sōji's finding for it (hint, rule, holds, levels) and its git state.

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: git_status
title: Git state
description: Read-only git facts for a path: repository root, default branch, uncommitted changes, unmerged or unpushed work, locked worktree, and the main worktree it belongs to.

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: open_files
title: Open files
description: Processes with a file open under a path or working in it (lsof records).

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: top_processes
title: Top processes
description: The top processes by CPU or memory: pid, parent pid, user id, CPU %, memory, age and command line. GPU use isn't measured; sort "gpu" orders by CPU.

name: process_info
title: About a process
description: One process: pid, parent pid, user id, CPU %, memory, age and command line.

name: agent_activity
title: Coding agent activity
description: When coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others on this Mac) last worked in a path, in a folder inside it, or in a folder that contains it.

path.description: Absolute path; ~ is the home folder

name: submit_findings
title: Submit findings
description: Your answer to Sōji. Call it once, with everything you found; Sōji verifies, measures and guards every item itself. Disk runs send findings; process runs send processVerdicts.

path.description: Absolute path of the folder or file

group.description: One of Sōji's groups, or a new one that names the thing itself

recommendation.description: remove: comes back on its own; trash: does not, but is not worth keeping; keep: the user still needs it; review: the user should decide

regenerable.description: True when it comes back on its own after removal (comesBack rebuilds or downloads)

comesBack.description: How it comes back: rebuilds (made again locally), downloads (fetched again), gone (lost)

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure you are of this judgment

levels.description: Which cleanup levels take it, and after how many idle hours. Leave every level out (keep only reason) for never

careful.description: Idle hours before this level takes it; 0 is now. Leave out: this level doesn't take it

balanced.description: Idle hours before this level takes it; 0 is now. Leave out: this level doesn't take it

aggressive.description: Idle hours before this level takes it; 0 is now. Leave out: this level doesn't take it

reason.description: One plain line the user reads

whatItIs.description: One plain line on what it is

whySafe.description: One plain line on why removing it loses nothing the user needs

howItComesBack.description: One plain line on how it comes back, if it does

inUseEvidence.description: For keep: what shows it is still in use

projectExists.description: Whether the project it belongs to still exists

gitState.description: What git_status showed; shown to the user, never used to tick

minLevel.description: The least aggressive cleanup level at which you would clean it

cleanCommand.description: The tool's official clean command, as argv

command.description: Command line, as process_info showed it

explanation.description: One plain line on what the process is

suggestion.description: quit: safe to quit; leave: let it run; never: must not be quit

reason.description: Why, in one or two plain lines

confidence.description: 0 to 1: how sure you are of this judgment
